'''Robert Martin Groves''' (born September 27, 1948)<ref name=wapost>{{cite news |title=Groves brings scholarly depth to bear in leading census, winning over critics |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2010/03/30/AR2010033003675_pf.html |author=Morello, Carol |newspaper=[[Washington Post]] |date=2010-03-31 |access-date=2010-10-02 |page=A15}}</ref> is an American [[sociology|sociologist]] and [[survey methodology]] scholar, currently serving as the senior advisor to the president of Georgetown University, following a term as interim president of [[Georgetown University]] from November 2024 to July 2026.

He served as executive vice president and provost of Georgetown University from August 2012 to November 2024 and as the 23rd [[director of the United States Census Bureau]] from 2009 to 2012.

==Early life and education==
Groves was born in [[Kansas City, Missouri]], and grew up in [[Metairie, Louisiana]]. He graduated in 1966 from [[De La Salle High School (New Orleans)|De La Salle High School]] in [[New Orleans|New Orleans, Louisiana]].<ref name=wapost/><ref name="nolaearly">{{cite web |url=http://www.nola.com/news/?/base/news-2/125065981636430.xml&coll=1 |work=[[Nola.com]] |title=Census boss plans special efforts
 |date=August 19, 2009 |access-date=2010-01-01 |author=Michelle Krupa}}</ref>

In 1970, Groves graduated ''[[summa cum laude]]'' and [[Phi Beta Kappa]] from [[Dartmouth College]], receiving a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree with a major in [[sociology]].<ref name="WashPost1">{{cite news |author=Rucker, Philip |date=2009-04-02 |title=Transportation and Education Depts. Get Key Nominees |url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/44/2009/04/02/transportation_and_education_d.html?wprss=44 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130205172852/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/44/2009/04/02/transportation_and_education_d.html?wprss=44 |archive-date=February 5, 2013 |access-date=2009-04-03 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}}</ref><ref name=NYTBio>{{cite news|author=Stout, David |title=Former Census Official Reportedly in Line to Head Agency  | newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=2009-04-02 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/04/03/washington/03census.html?ref=politics |access-date=2009-04-02}}</ref> He later received two [[Master of Arts|Master of Arts degrees]] (sociology and [[statistics]], both 1973) and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (sociology, 1975) from the [[University of Michigan]].<ref name=NYTBio/><ref name=CV>{{cite web |url=http://www.psc.isr.umich.edu/people/cv/groves_robert_cv.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae Robert M. Groves |access-date=2010-01-01 |date= September 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060901075920/http://www.psc.isr.umich.edu/people/cv/groves_robert_cv.pdf|archive-date=2006-09-01|url-status=dead }}
</ref>

==Academic career==
For much of his career, starting in 1975, Groves worked as a [[research professor]] in [[Statistical survey|survey]] [[Survey Methodology|methodology]] at the [[University of Michigan]]. He was also a researcher in the [[Joint Program in Survey Methodology]], housed at the [[University of Maryland, College Park]]. In August 2012, he became the Provost of [[Georgetown University]], succeeding [[James J. O'Donnell]]<ref name="georgetown-voice-april-2012">{{cite web |url=http://blog.georgetownvoice.com/2012/04/10/u-s-census-bureau-director-robert-groves-to-be-next-provost |title=U.S. Census Bureau director Robert Groves to be next Provost {{!}} Vox Populi |website=blog.georgetownvoice.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141104180929/http://blog.georgetownvoice.com/2012/04/10/u-s-census-bureau-director-robert-groves-to-be-next-provost/ |archive-date=2014-11-04}}</ref> and is also the Gerard J. Campbell, S.J. Professor in the Math and Statistics Department as well as the Sociology Department.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Provost Robert Groves |url=https://provost.georgetown.edu/about/robert-groves/ |access-date=August 22, 2023 |website=Georgetown University}}</ref>

In 1982 Groves was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].<ref>[http://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm View/Search Fellows of the ASA] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160616161612/https://www.amstat.org/awards/fellowslist.cfm |date=2016-06-16 }}, accessed 2016-10-15.</ref> He was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2011 and is a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name="georgetown-voice-april-2012" />

==Government career==
When Groves was an associate director at the [[United States Census Bureau]] in the early 1990s, he argued that potentially millions of [[Minority group|minorities]] who typically voted [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] were being undercounted. Groves advocated for the use of statistical adjustments to account for this discrepancy. [[George H. W. Bush]]'s [[U.S. Secretary of Commerce|Commerce Secretary]] [[Robert Mosbacher]] blocked this suggestion. The Census Bureau is a component of the [[U.S. Department of Commerce]].<ref name=NYTBio/>

On April 2, 2009, Groves was nominated by President [[Barack Obama]] to head the Census Bureau.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2009/04/02/AR2009040203725.html |title=With 2010 Census Looming, Obama Chooses Survey Expert to Run Bureau |author=O'Keefe, Ed |date=2009-04-03 |access-date=2009-04-03 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |page=A17}}</ref>  During his confirmation hearings, Republican [[U.S. Senator|senators]] raised concerns based on Groves' previous actions that he would apply statistical adjustments to populations believed to be undercounted, thereby inflating their numbers and affecting the apportionment of congressional seats.  Groves ruled out the use of statistical adjustments during the hearings and his nomination quickly proceeded to the full Senate in May.  However, senators [[Richard Shelby]] and [[David Vitter]] continued to delay his confirmation due to lingering worries regarding statistical adjustments.  They also sought assurance from the [[Obama administration]] that the controversial community group [[Association of Community Organizations for Reform Now|ACORN]] would not be involved in grassroots outreach related to the [[2010 United States Census|2010 Census]].  On July 13, 2009, after several weeks of opposition by the two senators, [[Senate majority leader]] [[Harry Reid]] used a procedural motion to force a vote that confirmed Groves, 76–15.<ref name="GrovesConfirmedAP">{{cite web|url=https://www.google.com/hostednews/ap/article/ALeqM5hXx_Z-rGJjGfdC5MFYs7vCq4fQzwD99DRK2O6 |title=Senate confirms Obama's pick to lead 2010 census |author=Yen, Hope |date=2009-07-13 |access-date=2009-07-13 |publisher=[[Associated Press]] }}{{dead link|date=June 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>  He took office July 15, 2009.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.census.gov/Press-Release/www/releases/pdf/RobertGrovesbio.pdf |title=Robert M. Groves, Director |access-date=2010-01-01 |date=July 16, 2009 |publisher=[[U.S. Census Bureau]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090830222449/http://www.census.gov/Press-Release/www/releases/pdf/RobertGrovesbio.pdf|archive-date=2009-08-30|url-status=dead }} 
</ref><ref>
{{cite web |title=History: Robert M. Groves |url=https://www.census.gov/history/www/director_biographies/013999.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090731231504/http://www.census.gov/history/www/director_biographies/013999.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 31, 2009 |date=July 20, 2009 |publisher=[[United States Census Bureau]] |access-date=22 July 2009 }}</ref>

On June 13, 2014, President Obama announced his appointment of Groves to the [[National Science Board]] of the [[National Science Foundation]].<ref>[https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2014/06/13/president-obama-announces-more-key-administration-posts-0 www.whitehouse.gov]</ref>

==Publishing history==
Groves is the author of several books, including:
* ''Surveying Victims'' (2008) {{ISBN|0-309-11598-1}}
* ''Survey Errors and Survey Costs'' (2004) first published in 1989 {{ISBN|0-471-67851-1}}, and named "one of the 50 most influential books in survey research" by the [[American Association for Public Opinion Research]]<ref name=":0" />
* ''Survey Methodology'' (2010) Second edition of the (2004) first edition {{ISBN|0-471-48348-6}}
* ''Survey Nonresponse'' (2001) {{ISBN|0-471-39627-3}}
* ''Nonresponse in Household Interview Surveys'' (1998) {{ISBN|0-471-18245-1}}

Groves is the editor of several books, including:
* ''Measurement Errors in Surveys'' (2004) {{ISBN|0-471-69280-8}}
* ''Telephone Survey Methodology'' (2001) {{ISBN|0-471-20956-2}}
